response: Yes, sex can affect the outcome of laparoscopic cholecystectomy. According to available data, laparoscopic cholecystectomy is often more challenging in men due to the presence of more adhesions and inflammation. This can lead to higher conversion rates and more postoperative complications in male patients. However, optimized planning and a more experienced operating surgeon may help overcome these problems and improve outcomes for men undergoing laparoscopic cholecystectomy.
